tasks.title: Build an isolated LinkedIn profile adapter with one-time HAR reconnaissance
tasks.summary: Use a one-time, local, authorized HAR review only to understand browser request/response data shape for developer reconnaissance; do not replay requests or use captured credentials/session tokens. Implement a separate LinkedIn profile adapter that accepts operator-provided profile JSON and maps only fields present in the input into the shared profile contract, with preview and provenance. Do not build automated LinkedIn endpoint scraping or a recurring HAR ingestion feature. If the HAR contains private/API endpoints requiring authenticated replay or access-control workarounds, stop at documenting the limitation. Keep LinkedIn source IDs namespaced separately from JobVision, require explicit human approval before persistence if persistence is in scope, and preserve JobVision adapter, routes, schema, config, schedules, and default behavior. Add synthetic parser/preview tests and JobVision regression checks without Docker/network; do not inspect .env or place real HAR/person data in code, fixtures, logs, or docs.

tasks.title: Define the HR dashboard and extensible filter contract
tasks.summary: After TASK-HR-001 is DONE, inspect the existing HR module, data model, permissions, and dashboard surfaces. Define dashboard acceptance criteria and an Elasticsearch-first filter contract for filter metadata/options, validated operators and values, sorting, pagination, and facets/aggregations. The dashboard must query an Elasticsearch HR read-model/index; adding a supported filter must not require adding a relational database column or changing the transactional database schema. Design a safe, extensible index document/mapping strategy for new searchable attributes (for example controlled dynamic templates or a typed attributes object), while preventing mapping explosion and arbitrary client-supplied query DSL. Document source-of-truth, ingestion/synchronization and freshness, mapping version/reindex strategy, authorization/PII controls, and unsupported-field behavior. Shape the HR index so it can later be exposed as a separately authorized RAG collection without coupling the dashboard to chatbot code; RAG implementation is not part of this task. Do not modify the Sima application in this design task.

tasks.title: Implement the HR dashboard with extensible filters
tasks.summary: Implement and test the conventional HR dashboard against the approved TASK-HR-002 contract. Elasticsearch is the dashboard query/read-model backend; do not add relational database columns or alter transactional schema just to support new dashboard filters. Make filter additions a small, well-defined configuration/indexing/query change using validated allowlisted fields/operators and the approved extensible mapping strategy; never accept arbitrary client Elasticsearch DSL. Preserve existing HR permissions, source synchronization/freshness expectations, and unrelated local changes. Keep the index compatible with later separately authorized RAG reuse, but do not implement RAG in this task. Only stage files belonging to this task, and do not claim or change any TASK-NNN work.
